status: PROTOTYPE — not part of the released Atlas. Proposal for a v0.4 gate; nothing here is approved content.
extends_note: Atlas items (r-*, p-*, i-*), territories (t-*), outputs (out-*) and sources (s-*) are read from data/atlas.json at runtime and are not duplicated here. Hosting, territory and output links of Atlas items are derived from their existing atlas.json fields; they are not restated.

verification_default.statement: Each cited passage was read at its pinned commit by an AI assistant during this proposal. This is not human verification. Human verification of every public relationship is pending and is a v0.4 acceptance criterion.

classes.label: TECHNICAL DEPENDENCY
classes.definition: One item's code or data pipeline reads, loads or forks another item's artifact, as documented by the dependent item's own pinned source.

classes.label: STRUCTURAL
classes.definition: Containment or attachment documented in a record: a repository hosts an item, an item has an output. Never implies data exchange.

classes.label: METHODOLOGICAL
classes.definition: An item applies a named method or uses a named dataset, or is a declared extension of another item's research design, as stated in its source.

classes.label: TERRITORIAL
classes.definition: An item is situated in a territory, or a territory lies within another, as stated by a source. Overlap is never computed or inferred.

classes.label: HYPOTHETICAL
classes.definition: A future application named by a source as possible but not undertaken. It never counts as a dependency and is hidden until the reader turns it on.

classes.label: CONCEPTUAL (ANALYST-DEFINED)
classes.definition: An association proposed by the Atlas analyst, not stated by either item's sources. Not evidence. Development inventory only; never in the public graph.

predicates.label: depends on
predicates.definition: The source item cannot run or build without the target item's artifact at a pinned version.
predicates.required_evidence: A pinned source in the dependent item that names the target and the pinned version it loads.
predicates.limits: Says nothing about the scientific validity of either item. A dependency on a pinned version is not a dependency on the target's current state.
inference_rules: Not transitive for claims: what A may claim does not grow because B is a dependency.
Never inferred from shared authorship, territory or vocabulary.

predicates.label: reads outputs of
predicates.definition: The source item ingests a published output of the target item (data values, files) through a documented extraction.
predicates.required_evidence: A pinned provenance record in the consumer naming the producer, the producer commit and the fields read.
predicates.limits: The consumer inherits the producer's claim ceiling for the values it reads. Consumption does not validate the producer, and the producer's conclusions do not become the consumer's.
inference_rules: Only the documented subset is consumed; never generalise to all outputs.
Labels or verdicts not stated as consumed are not consumed.

predicates.label: derived from
predicates.definition: The source item is a declared fork or derivative edition of the target item's code base.
predicates.required_evidence: A pinned declaration in the derivative (e.g. a related-identifier `isDerivedFrom`, or README statement).
predicates.limits: Shared code does not transfer validation, results, versions or identifiers between the two.
inference_rules: A result of the origin is never a result of the derivative, or the reverse.

predicates.label: hosts
predicates.definition: The target item's files live inside the source item's repository.
predicates.required_evidence: A pinned source showing the hosted item's location; v0.3 `hosts` fields are reused as-is.
predicates.limits: Hosting is co-location of files. It does not imply the host's application reads, displays or depends on the hosted item.
inference_rules: Never read as data exchange. Where a source states isolation, a documented non-relationship is recorded.

predicates.label: extends
predicates.definition: The source item is a declared research extension of the target, reusing its setting or infrastructure under its own question.
predicates.required_evidence: A pinned statement in the extension that names the base study and the boundary between them.
predicates.limits: An extension does not revise, confirm or refute the base study. Their questions, results and outputs stay separate (v0.3 A4).
inference_rules: Never combine the two items' results or verdicts.

predicates.label: applies method
predicates.definition: The item's methodology source states that it applies the named method.
predicates.limits: Two items applying one method do not share configuration, inputs, calibration or validity.
inference_rules: ‘Shares method’ is never stored. It is read only as two separate applies_method edges, each with its own source.

predicates.label: uses dataset
predicates.definition: The item's source states that it uses a product of the named dataset; the edge records which extract, product or vintage.
predicates.required_evidence: A pinned source naming the dataset and, where stated, the extract, product or retrieval date.
predicates.limits: Items using one dataset family usually use different extracts, products or vintages. A common dataset does not establish comparability or scientific agreement.
inference_rules: The extract note on each edge must be read before comparing items.

predicates.label: situated in
predicates.definition: The item's source places its study area, network or case in the territory.
predicates.required_evidence: For Atlas items, the v0.3 territory record; for others, a pinned source naming the area.
predicates.limits: A territory label is not geometry. Two items in one territory did not necessarily study the same area, period or phenomenon.
inference_rules: Never infer overlap or comparability from a shared territory.

predicates.label: lies within
predicates.definition: A source places the smaller territory inside the larger one (an official code, or the municipality named by the source).
predicates.required_evidence: A source stating the containment; no geometry is intersected by the Atlas.
predicates.limits: Containment only. Overlap between sibling territories is not computed and not asserted.
inference_rules: Sibling territories inside one parent are not thereby adjacent or overlapping.

predicates.label: has output
predicates.limits: Unchanged from v0.3: every output belongs to exactly one item.

predicates.label: possible future application to
predicates.direction: source of the idea → possible target
predicates.definition: A source names the target as a possible application domain that has not been undertaken.
predicates.required_evidence: A pinned source that names the target and states the condition (e.g. validation) that would be required.
predicates.limits: Not a dependency, not planned work, not evidence. Shown only when the reader turns hypothetical relations on.
inference_rules: Must never be counted in answers about dependencies or use.

predicates.label: conceptually related to (analyst)
predicates.definition: An analyst-defined association that no source states.
predicates.required_evidence: A written analyst rationale and the sources that show the two items differ.
predicates.limits: Not evidence and not a methodological equivalence. Development inventory only.
inference_rules: Never displayed in the public graph.

rejected_predicates.reason: Stored ‘shares’ edges assert an equivalence the sources do not make. The same answer is read from two independent applies_method, situated_in or uses_dataset edges, each carrying its own extract note and source.
Relatedness of research questions has no defensible, source-based test. It would be analyst-defined in every case.
No source in the inventory contrasts two items; a contrast drawn by the Atlas would be a comparison, which v0.3 non-goal 7 forbids.
Already expressed by the v0.3 one-parent fields (evidence.research_id, finding.research_id). Duplicating them as graph edges adds nodes, not meaning; the dossier remains the place to read them.
No documented case in the inventory.
No defensible method exists. Relationship classes are categorical and are not ranked.

node_kinds.label: RESEARCH ITEM
node_kinds.note: v0.3 classes kept: documented research, experiment, research platform, instrument. A candidate is not an admitted Atlas item.

node_kinds.label: METHOD
node_kinds.note: Named method as stated by an item's methodology source.

node_kinds.label: DATASET
node_kinds.note: A dataset family; each edge records the extract, product or vintage used.

node_kinds.label: TERRITORY
node_kinds.note: v0.3 territory records, plus candidate territories named by candidate items. Text, not geometry.

evidence.quote_summary: Lens ‘reads’ 14 outdoor assets' UTCI values in a read-only, provenance-labelled way; never modifies HATI or carries forward its feasibility labels.
Source commit f02f5f6…; files pilot_assets.csv and phase2_asset_thermal_exposure.csv; no interpolation.
Machine-readable record: commit, fields used, filter indoor_outdoor == 'outdoor', limitations.

limits: Only the pilot (Layer A, release-locked) is read; the pedestrian heat extension is not.
Only 14 outdoor assets on one modelled day; not a city-wide surface and never interpolated.
HATI's feasibility and recommendation labels are not consumed, so the Lens does not inherit HATI's verdicts.
Reading HATI values does not validate HATI, and HATI's preprint result is not a Lens finding.
